transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you’d like to talk about?

Well, yes… I came because I seem to spend an awful lot of time checking things. Mostly my folders and drawers, and those little labeled boxes I keep for papers and keepsakes. I’ll open one to make sure something important is still there, and then a few minutes later I’m back opening it again, as if it might have walked off.

It sounds silly when I say it out loud. My daughter bought me a label maker years ago—lovely thing, really—and I thought being organized would help, but now I’m just going in and out of the same places all day. It’s gotten to be too much.
When you check your folders and drawers, do you have a specific worry or thought that comes up, like a fear that something bad will happen if you don’t check?

Yes… yes, there is a thought. It isn’t always sensible, and I know that, but it sort of needles at me. I’ll think, what if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers by mistake, or put one of the family recipes in the wrong little box?

And then I feel just awful, like I’ve been terribly careless. My husband kept things in such a particular way—well, not everything, he could never find his glasses—but important papers, he was careful with those. So even if part of me knows I probably didn’t do anything wrong, I can’t seem to just let the thought pass.
Do these thoughts upset you and feel out of line with how you normally think, or do they seem to just fit with your usual way of thinking?

They do upset me, yes. I mean, I know better, really I do… papers don’t just vanish because I didn’t look in a folder for ten minutes. But the thought keeps needling me anyway—what if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong little box?

It feels out of line, I suppose. I wasn’t always like this. I used to keep things tidy enough, though my mother would have said my cupboards were another matter. But now once that thought comes in, I can’t seem to let it pass. I feel as if I’ve done something terribly careless, even when I can’t prove I’ve done anything at all.

When you feel that urge to check your folders or boxes, does it come with a feeling of anxiety or distress that you’re trying to reduce by checking, or does it feel more like something needs to be done a certain way to feel right?

It’s more that I feel driven to check, I suppose. I’ll open the same folder or drawer, or one of those little labeled boxes, just to make sure the important papers or keepsakes are still where I left them. And then—this is the ridiculous part—I may have checked it only a few minutes before, but I’ll go back and do it again.

I do get upset if I don’t, though I can’t always say it’s one neat feeling. My sister used to say I was the organized one, because I kept labels on everything, but now the labels almost make it worse because I think, “Well, if it has a proper place, I’d better make sure it’s in that place.” So I spend far too much of the day opening and closing things.

Are the thoughts that come to you when you’re checking your folders or boxes something you experience as separate from your usual stream of thoughts—like they pop into your mind uninvited and don’t really sound like you?

Well… yes, in a way. It’s not like I sit down and decide to worry about it. It just pops up and keeps needling at me, even when I know better.

I’ll be doing something ordinary—making tea, or looking for a pen, though I can never find the good pens when I need them—and suddenly I’ll think, “What if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers?” Or, “What if I put one of the family recipes in the wrong box?” And then I can’t seem to let it go. It feels like I’ve done something terribly careless, even if I don’t have any real reason to think so.
Do these thoughts feel foreign or inconsistent with who you are as a person, or do they feel more like they fit with how you normally think?

They feel inconsistent with me, I think. I mean, I know better—of course papers don’t just disappear because I didn’t stare at the folder long enough. But the thought keeps needling at me anyway, like maybe I threw away my husband’s old tax papers, or put one of the family recipes in the wrong box.

And then I can’t just let it pass. I feel as if I’ve done something terribly careless, even when I don’t really have any reason to think I did. It’s not how I used to be… I used to be careful, yes, but not like this.
When these thoughts come up, do you feel you have to perform the checking behavior to prevent something bad from happening, or to reduce the discomfort they cause?

Yes… I think it’s mostly to settle that awful discomfort. I feel like I have to check, or I can’t move on with the day. I’ll open the same folder, the same drawer, those labeled boxes—sometimes I’ve only just looked a few minutes before—and I still have to make sure the papers or little keepsakes are where I left them.

It sounds silly when I say it out loud. My niece once bought me these pretty labels for Christmas, very neat little things, and at the time I thought they’d help. But now I spend far too much time opening and closing everything. It’s not really useful anymore, it’s just… I feel driven to do it.
